solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Please don't panic, clumsily engaging gear

indicators.note: engaging means taking hold of something within, so the gear is set inside the jumbled letters
done clumsily, the letters of panic are fumbled into a new order

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stay calm while fumbling to put a car into gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please don't' is the plea to stop, not politeness; 'clumsily' and 'engaging' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning stop doing that is a fair stand-in for a plea that someone not continue.

clue.text: Soup container: boil without lid

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: losing its lid in a down clue means the top letter of the word for boil is taken off

parts.note: to rage is to boil with anger

explanation.surface: Instructions for cooking soup: put it in a container and boil it uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lid' drops the R from RAGE, leaving AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup or broth is called by this French culinary term.

clue.text: Depressing advice to overenthusiastic supporters?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, telling fans who make too much noise to shout less

explanation.surface: A gloomy thought about telling over-keen fans to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into CHEER LESS, an instruction to fans; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreary and gloomy that offers no comfort is depressing in mood.

clue.text: A long time redeveloping a region

indicators.note: redeveloping means rebuilding in a new form, so the letters of a region are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regenerating a run-down region takes ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period after the Bronze Age lasted many centuries, so it is an era or long time.

clue.text: Very minor leader deposed, causing sensation

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and deposing it removes it

parts.note: titchy is informal British for very small

explanation.surface: A very minor leader is overthrown, which creates a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader deposed' takes the first T from TITCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritating prickle on the skin is a sensation, and something prickly produces one.

clue.text: Do over

parts.note: a bash is a party or do
up can mean over, as in time is up

explanation.surface: Two words that read as a request to repeat something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition (to do someone over is to beat them up) and also the wordplay, a party followed by finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To do over is British slang for assaulting someone, the same as beating them violently.

clue.text: She performs on front of stage, among characters from cast

indicators.note: among places the following pieces inside the rearranged letters
the letters taken from cast are rearranged to make a new word

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the front of stage is its first letter

explanation.surface: A performer stands at the front of the stage among the rest of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters from' makes ACTS, the outer piece that 'among' fills.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs on stage or screen is described by this term.

clue.text: Jack is outwardly very sexy

indicators.note: being outward, the word for very sexy wraps around is

parts.note: hot means very sexy

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack has a very sexy appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack up a car is to raise or lift it, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Drink up and hang around for a piece of cake

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to hover is to hang around

explanation.surface: Finish your drink and linger over a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily achieved is idiomatically a pushover, just as a doddle is a piece of cake.

clue.text: Spent season meandering at first on lake in south of France

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the French word

parts.note: sud is French for south

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next
at first takes the opening letter of meandering

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker spent summer wandering by a lake in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: To summer somewhere is to pass the warm season there, so the past tense means spent that season.

clue.text: Part of Europe where Parisian wears fancy winter clothes

indicators.note: the Parisian word wears the clothes, so the jumbled letters go around it
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ou is French for where, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A Parisian dresses in elaborate winter clothes in some part of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges WINTER CLOTHES and 'wears' wraps them round OU.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg are collectively known by this name for a region of Europe.

clue.text: Note principal features of European referendum: a good deal for the country

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: the principal or leading features of these words are their first letters

parts.note: many means a good deal of

explanation.surface: A political note on a European referendum offering the country a good deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation, Germany is an example of a country.

clue.text: Making comeback as alternative band recruits singular top musician

indicators.note: coming back means the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: recruiting takes someone into the group, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a team is a band of people
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A band making a comeback recruits a single top musician as an alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recruits' gives TSEAM; with OR first, 'Making comeback' reverses ORTSEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A great conductor or virtuoso is hailed with this Italian title for a master.

clue.text: Producer's request: character should omit line

parts.note: to beg is to request

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so the line is removed

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A film producer asks that a character be cut from the script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should omit' drops L from LETTER to leave ETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who begets is a father or producer of offspring, an old word for an originator.

clue.text: Bulldoze each road in urban area

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the urban area

parts.note: a town is an urban area

explanation.surface: Each road in a built-up area is to be bulldozed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a building is to demolish it, a phrasal verb with the same meaning.

clue.text: Medic at last probes painful scratch

indicators.note: probing means pushing into something, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: sore means painful

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of medic

explanation.surface: A doctor finally examines a painful scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a cut or scratch made on a surface.

clue.text: Upsets Open University, with grants being regularly cut

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden

indicators.note: regularly cut means every other letter is removed, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: The Open University is upset that its grants keep being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' looks like the institution but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a ruling or a boat is to upset it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Political extremists fear a Republican will get in

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so these letters go inside

parts.note: fright is fear

explanation.surface: Extremists fear that a Republican will be elected.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme right wing of politics is a name for the most reactionary extremists.

clue.text: Fabulous writer circulating main work

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the word for main is turned backwards

parts.note: the main is the open sea
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A wonderful writer's major work is being circulated.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller wrote fables, so he is literally a writer of fables.

clue.text: Final character expelled from Cornwall town getting punishment

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the county at the far south-west tip of England
Z is the final character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out of a Cornish town is being punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled from' takes Z out of PENZANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-imposed suffering done to atone for wrongdoing, a kind of punishment.

clue.text: Author with Irish name

parts.note: and means with or plus
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A writer bearing an Irish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish writer of fairy tales, an author.

clue.text: Twice jumping up when bitten by bug? That's ludicrous

indicators.note: bitten by means held in the bug's jaws, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to bug is to annoy or rile

indicators.note: in a down clue, jumping up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: Leaping up twice when bitten by an insect looks laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping up' makes SIB; bis, Latin for twice, is printed on music to call for a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, deserving to be laughed at.

clue.text: Club attracts female swimmer

indicators.note: attracts means draws to itself, so the next piece follows on

parts.note: a bat is a club
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A sports club appeals to a woman who swims.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bathing in the sea or a pool is a swimmer.

clue.text: Distilled brandy put in wine

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: red is a wine
fine is a French brandy

explanation.surface: A distilled spirit like brandy is added to wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined means purified, as distilled spirits are cleansed of impurities.

clue.text: Financier's case containing this writer's money

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the next piece goes within
the case of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: this writer's means I have, contracted

explanation.surface: A financier's briefcase holds this writer's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is the setter saying I've.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pound note is British slang for a sum of money.

clue.text: Island on a lake, perched near area in old Gallic region

indicators.note: in an across clue, island on means the island letter follows what comes after
near means next to, so the area letter is placed alongside

parts.note: sat means perched

explanation.surface: An island on a lake is perched near an area in old Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old Latin name for Alsace, a region in eastern France once part of Gaul.

clue.text: Inventive fellow in total disarray

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words total disarray

explanation.surface: An inventor's affairs are in total chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Aldis invented the signalling lamp named after him, used at sea, so he is a fellow who invented things.

clue.text: Avoided having offer of spacious on-board accommodation?

definitions.meaning: steered clear of, kept away from

definitions.text: having offer of spacious on-board accommodation?
definitions.meaning: a berth is a bed on a ship, so a wide one is roomy cabin space offered

explanation.surface: Someone was kept at a distance after being offered roomy shipboard accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of a ship's berth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for keeping well clear of someone or something describes avoidance.

clue.text: Shoot at wretch knocked over by cop

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rat is a wretch
to cop is to get or catch

explanation.surface: A villain is knocked over by a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is what one shoots at, the noun for an aim or goal.

clue.text: Examiner wanted dunces to have time out of class

parts.note: asses are fools or dunces

indicators.note: out of means the time letter is removed

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind

explanation.surface: An examiner wants dull pupils to have time out of class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes T from SORT, leaving SOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or examines work, a synonym for an examiner.
